slot.brief: Ask which radical species initiates ozone decomposition in the stratosphere and identify the catalytic chain steps; include one statement about CFCs vs NOx.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding the catalytic depletion of stratospheric ozone by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and nitrogen oxides ($\text{NO}_x$) is INCORRECT?
options: The catalytic cycle is initiated by chlorine free radicals ($\dot{\text{Cl}}$) generated via UV photolysis of CFCs.
The propagation step that regenerates the chlorine radical is $\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}(g) + \text{O}(g) \rightarrow \dot{\text{Cl}}(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$.
Nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$) emitted from supersonic jets depletes ozone via the propagation step $\text{NO}(g) + \text{O}_3(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$.
Unlike CFCs, which act catalytically, ozone breakdown by $\text{NO}$ is stoichiometric because $\text{NO}_2$ cannot regenerate $\text{NO}$.

verdicts.working: Cl cycle: CF2Cl2 --UV--> Cl•; Cl• + O3 → ClO• + O2; ClO• + O → Cl• + O2 (A, B correct). NO cycle: NO + O3 → NO2 + O2 (C correct), then NO2 + O → NO + O2 regenerates NO, so NO also acts catalytically. Hence statement D is false.

working:
1. **CFC mechanism:** In the stratosphere, chlorofluorocarbons (such as $\text{CF}_2\text{Cl}_2$) undergo photolysis under UV radiation to produce chlorine radicals:$$\text{CF}_2\text{Cl}_2(g) \xrightarrow{h\nu} \dot{\text{Cl}}(g) + \dot{\text{C}}\text{F}_2\text{Cl}(g)$$This initiates the catalytic breakdown cycle. Hence, statement A is correct.

2. **CFC propagation steps:**$$\dot{\text{Cl}}(g) + \text{O}_3(g) \rightarrow \text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$$$$\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}}(g) + \text{O}(g) \rightarrow \dot{\text{Cl}}(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$$The second step produces molecular oxygen and regenerates the active $\dot{\text{Cl}}$ radical, allowing a single radical to destroy thousands of ozone molecules. Hence, statement B is correct.

3. **$\text{NO}_x$ mechanism:** Nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$) from supersonic jet exhausts destroys ozone via a two-step catalytic cycle:$$\text{NO}(g) + \text{O}_3(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$$$$\text{NO}_2(g) + \text{O}(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$$Net reaction: $\text{O}_3(g) + \text{O}(g) \rightarrow 2\text{O}_2(g)$. Statement C correctly identifies the first propagation step.

4. Because $\text{NO}_2$ reacts with atomic oxygen to regenerate $\text{NO}$, $\text{NO}$ also acts as a homogeneous catalyst rather than being consumed stoichiometrically. Statement D falsely claims that the reaction is stoichiometric and non-regenerative.

Independent check: Cl cycle: CF2Cl2 --UV--> Cl•; Cl• + O3 → ClO• + O2; ClO• + O → Cl• + O2 (A, B correct). NO cycle: NO + O3 → NO2 + O2 (C correct), then NO2 + O → NO + O2 regenerates NO, so NO also acts catalytically. Hence statement D is false.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A is a true statement: a student may mistakenly choose it by thinking fluorine radicals ($\dot{\text{F}}$) initiate the cycle instead of $\dot{\text{Cl}}$ (C–F bonds are too strong to be broken by stratospheric UV).
Option B is a true statement: a student may mistakenly believe this is termination rather than propagation, or confuse it with ozone reaction directly ($\text{Cl}\dot{\text{O}} + \text{O}_3$).
Option C is a true statement: a student unaware that $\text{NO}$ acts catalytically in ozone depletion may mistake this for an incorrect reaction.
